questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: ............ is unstable at cooking temperature, whereas the control of sweetness of food is difficult while using.........
questions.solution:
Aspartame is an artificial sweetener that is unstable at cooking temperatures because it decomposes upon heating, which limits its use to cold foods and drinks.

Alitame is a high-potency artificial sweetener that is extremely sweet, making it difficult to control the sweetness of food products when used as a sweetening agent.

Answer: Aspartame and alitame

Barbiturates are a class of drugs that act as central nervous system depressants. They are primarily used as sedatives, hypnotics, and anticonvulsants. In the context of medical treatment, they are used to induce sleep, reduce anxiety, and manage seizures. Among the given options, they are used to treat conditions related to overactivity of the central nervous system, which is often associated with the clinical management of depression or anxiety-related insomnia, though they are not antidepressants themselves. questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following artificial sweeteners can be used in soft drinks only?
questions.solution:
Aspartame is the most successful and widely used artificial sweetener. It is roughly 100 times as sweet as cane sugar. Its use is limited to cold foods and soft drinks because it is unstable at cooking temperatures and decomposes during baking or cooking. Therefore, it is used only in soft drinks and cold foods.

Answer: Aspartame

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is added to soaps to impart antiseptic properties?
questions.solution:
Soaps are sodium or potassium salts of long-chain fatty acids. To impart antiseptic properties to soaps, certain chemicals are added.

Bithional, also known as bithionol, is a chemical compound added to soaps to reduce the odor produced by bacterial decomposition of organic matter on the skin and to provide antiseptic action.

Iodine is an antiseptic but is typically used as a tincture or solution, not added to soaps for this purpose. Furacine is an antibiotic ointment. Terpineol is used in soaps for fragrance.

Answer: Bithional

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is used as a drug to reduce fever?
questions.solution:
Drugs used to reduce fever are known as antipyretics. These substances lower the body temperature during high fever by acting on the hypothalamus, which regulates body temperature.

Antibiotics are used to treat bacterial infections. Analgesics are used to relieve pain. Tranquilisers are used to treat mental diseases or stress.

Answer: Antipyretic

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Arrange the following artificial Sweetening agents in order of increasing sweetness.
Aspartame, Saccharin, Sucralose, Alitame
questions.solution:
The relative sweetness values of artificial sweetening agents compared to cane sugar are as follows:

Aspartame is approximately 100 times as sweet as cane sugar.

Saccharin is approximately 550 times as sweet as cane sugar.

Sucralose is approximately 600 times as sweet as cane sugar.

Alitame is approximately 2000 times as sweet as cane sugar.

Arranging these in increasing order of sweetness gives: Aspartame (100) < Saccharin (550) < Sucralose (600) < Alitame (2000).

Therefore, the order of increasing sweetness is Aspartame < Saccharin < Sucralose < Alitame, which is equivalent to Alitame > Sucralose > Saccharin > Aspartame.

Answer: Alitame > Sucralose > Saccharin > Aspartame

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following options represent the correct composition of dettol?
questions.solution:
Dettol is a common antiseptic used for cleaning wounds and skin. It is a mixture of chloroxylenol and terpineol in a suitable solvent. Chloroxylenol acts as the primary antiseptic agent, while terpineol acts as a solvent and also possesses some antiseptic properties.

Answer: Chloroxylenol and terpineol

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is not an antacid?
questions.solution:
Antacids are substances that neutralize excess stomach acid to relieve heartburn and indigestion. Common examples include aluminium hydroxide, magnesium hydroxide, cimetidine, and ranitidine.

Cimetidine and ranitidine are $H_{2}$-receptor antagonists that reduce acid production in the stomach, and they are widely used as antacids.

Aluminium hydroxide is a common inorganic antacid used to neutralize gastric acid.

Phenelzine is a monoamine oxidase inhibitor (MAOI) used as an antidepressant, not as an antacid.

Answer: Phenelzine
